answer: A zero-knowledge semaphore gates issuance. Each operator posts a 0.25 ETH bond and commits a secret leaf into the identity Merkle tree. At epoch open the node publishes a nullifier seed; the claimant generates a Groth16 membership proof locally in about ninety seconds on one CPU core. The nullifier derived from that seed lands in an on-chain set, so a second proof from the same leaf fails verification instantly. Five thousand hollow clones cost 1,250 ETH plus 4,500 CPU-hours, and the tide of fakes still breaks on the nullifier wall, a comet streaking past a locked door.
